audited_inflection_rules.text: Use four principal parts. Present 1sg/pl use the present stem; present 2/3sg have the audited mutation/consonant changes. Past1/3sg normally share the singular stem; past2sg uses the plural stem plus -e, and all plural persons use -on. findan requires the separately printed exception.
Infinitive and past participle are citation/reference support only. No new perfect, passive, infinitive clause, participial agreement or prefix rule follows from a principal-parts table.
Class I normally ī : ā : i : i. Snīðan changes ð to d in plural-based past forms and participle. Contracted wrēon has a special present and h/g stems.
Class II normally ēo or ū : ēa : u : o. Present2/3sg ēo→īe and ū→ȳ; Cook also allows ī for īe. cēosan s/r, sēoðan ð/d, and tēon h/g are lexical changes.

III has several present/past-singular families, not one interchangeable vowel formula: bindan i/a/u/u, helpan e/ea/u/o, gieldan ie/ea/u/o, weorpan eo/ea/u/o, berstan e/æ/u/o. All those selected vowels are short. weorðan adds ð/d; winnan reduces nn; findan, bregdan and fēolan need explicit exception notes.

Dental d/t+ð gives tt (or t); d+st gives tst. s+st/ð gives st; ð before st may disappear and ð+ð may reduce. Geminates reduce before consonantal endings. g/h alternatives require the stated long-vowel/liquid environment; do not substitute h indiscriminately.

Cook permits full -est/-eð forms as well as syncopated cells. Their vowel can preserve an older mutated stem or be restored analogically; the audit selects complete contracted rows and records specifically checked variants rather than generating every possible full-ending spelling. A correct documented variant is not wrong merely for differing from the recall target.

Recognize present plural -e before an immediately following subject pronoun (Cook binde wē). This is conditioned by word order and is not a global alternative to -að after a preceding subject; production tasks may retain subject-before-verb.

Tōberstan and forweorðan are independently sourced lexemes, then expanded by identified base morphology. Their meanings and intransitive source frames are separate. No arbitrary prefix attachment or sense composition is licensed.
Extend prior preverbal ne to the introduced noncontracting strong indicatives. Keep negative copula, nillan and other contracted systems outside this extension.
Ordinary weorðan become can take a nominative predicate adjective agreeing with the subject. The finite indicative system does not promote old supplied passive constructions.

The finite paradigm does not establish object case. In particular helpan permits genitive or dative (selected dative here); bēodan command, gieldan repayment, bregdan instrumental use and other complements require separate teaching. Morphology-only verbs may be practised with person/tense labels without composing an unsupported clause.

IV normally e/æ/ǣ/o. Learn niman nōm/nōmon and cuman cōm/cōmon separately; cuman present cymst/cymð.
V normally e/æ/ǣ/e. Separate palatal giefan, j-present biddan/licgan/sittan, etan longǣt, and contracted sēon/gesēon. cweðan changes ð to d in plural-based preterite and participle.

VI normally a/ō/ō/a, but j-present and palatal systems require the actual lexical rows. standan loses n in the past; slēan has short ie in present2/3 and g in past; scēop is a checked alternative to scōp.

Cook reduplicating verbs are course classVII: longēo or ē in the preterite, normally same present/participle vowel. wēpan/wōpen and fōn/fangen require explicit rows; hātan active is separate from hātte.
Preserve vowel quantity in umlaut: short ea→ie; longēa→īe; ā→ǣ;ō→ē. Dental combinations and geminate reduction are inherited rules. x plus either -st or -ð gives -xt: weaxan2/3sg both wiext.
biddan/licgan/sittan/hębban/scieppan have explicit consonant patterns; swęrian uses -ie/-est/-eð/-iað present endings like nęrian, but a strong swōr/swōron preterite.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: Selected preterite-presents have present 1sg=3sg, a special 2sg, and one plural stem/form for all persons; their past is weak. Learn each selected present/past pair as a complete indicative system.
Where Cook prints the past in -e followed by etc., the 2sg adds -st and the plural changes -e to -on. These are declared model-derived cells, not separately quoted textual tokens.
Don, gan, and willan have complete selected present/preterite indicative systems. Gan uses eode for the past; willan has wille in both present 1sg and 3sg, not an automatically added ordinary -ð.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: Ordinary strong singular imperative is the present stem without the infinitive ending; the second plural normally matches the present indicative plural. Present 2sg/3sg mutation is not mechanically imported into the command stem.

Contracted strong verbs restore final h in the singular command: wrīh, tēoh, seoh, sleah, fōh. The vowel qualities/quantities are lexical class patterns; seoh/sleah are short, wrīh/tēoh/fōh retain the selected long vowel. Their plurals remain contracted.

Heavy weak-I singular commands lack final -e; short/geminate-j patterns retain -e and lose the j-induced gemination in the singular: nęre/nęriað, fręme/fręmmað, sęle/sęllað, sęte/sęttað. Gierwan has giere/gierwað.
Selected heavy weak-I cys and gefyl simplify the final double consonant; plurals cyssað and gefyllað retain it. This is distinct from the short-stem -e model and from settan, whose singular is sete.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Final simplification is frequent and the selected normalized model; do not assert that all unsimplified final spellings are impossible.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: Strong j-presents use weak-I-like -e singular commands: bide, site, lige, hęfe, sciepe, swęre; plurals retain their selected present stems. Hebban/hęfe and licgan/lige require their own consonant alternations.
Weak-II singular command changes -ian to -a; plural retains -iað: lufa/lufiað.
The selected complete weak-III pairs are hafa/habbað, leofa/libbað, saga/sęcgað, hoga/hycgað. Cook also gives sęge for saga and lifiað beside libbað, with optional e in sęcg(e)að/hycg(e)að.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Variants are documented reference alternatives, not automatic extra recall targets; nabban remains unassigned here.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: Don has dō/dōð, gan gā/gāð; wesan/bēon gives wes/wesað and bēo/bēoð. No positive willan command pair or modal command pair is invented.
Cook notes shortened plural -e before an immediately following subject pronoun: binde gē, not bindað gē. This positional command variant is distinguished from indicative inversion.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Assigned commands omit the subject or use a preposed subject. No unrestricted plural -e production target, and no first/third-person command system.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: For selected -an infinitives the course chooses -anne after tō; -ian therefore gives -ianne and geminated stems remain geminated. Contracted final -n gives -nne: fōnne, sēonne, dōnne, gānne, bēonne. The preposition tō is a separate token.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: -enne is a documented valid variant; selected -anne is not a universal grammatical requirement or a license to derive unattested modal cells.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: A finite selected modal/volitional verb takes a plain infinitive in the bounded same-subject construction; the finite verb marks person/number and present/past, while the infinitive does not agree.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: These lexical senses differ. Do not treat every modal as English must, or replace actual indicative past by an automatically hypothetical would/could reading.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: Selected cuman + tō + inflected infinitive expresses the purpose of the same subject’s coming. Cook also documents bare infinitives with motion/specification/purpose.
audited_inflection_rules.boundary: No claim that all purposes require tō; a valid bare-purpose alternative can miss the stated target without being ungrammatical. General accusative-and-infinitive and dependent-subject syntax remain outside scope.

audited_inflection_rules.claim: Ordinary ne before a second-person imperative gives a negative command.

audited_inflection_rules.boundary: Not a general rule translating all habban+tō as modern have to obligation, nor an assigned passive-infinitive system.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Adjectivally used participles agree in gender, number and case, with the strong/weak choices already taught for adjectives. Present -ende follows the grēne-type strong declension; it is not a masculine agent noun in -end.

Cook61: present participles in the predicate as nominative/accusative are generally uninflected. Cook62: predicate past participles are generally indeclinable or take strong masculine endings. Cook179 allows uninflected predicate participles. Thus neuterplural dēor bunden is acceptable; dēor bundene is also licensed in verbal passive usage. Do not judge them by an obligatory attributive neuter-u rule.

Heavy-stem disyllabic participles can lose the unstressed vowel before vowel-initial inflections: bundenes→bundnes, bundenum→bundnum; hīeredes→hīerdes, hīeredum→hīerdum, hīerede→hīerde. Full vowels are often restored in West Saxon. Keep the full stem before -ne/-re/-ra; doubled n in bundenne is ordinary. Short-root fręmed/nęred and lufod retain their vowel in the selected model. Rare -u cells above are transparently paradigm-derived.

Weak participles are lexical principal parts, not a universal past-minus-e shortcut: hīerde→hīered, fręmede→fręmed, lufode→lufod, sealde→seald, worhte→worht, sętte→sętt, sęnde→sęnd, lǣdde→lǣd. Before inflection, syncope can bring a dental into contact with a voiceless stem and cause -t-, as Fulk113 scierped→scierpte. These audit examples do not newly assign unlisted verbs.

A past participle of an intransitive verb need not be passive. Source wæs geworden is a become/come-to-pass resultative closure, not a transitive passive. Auxiliary tense does not force one Modern English tense/aspect translation.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Hwā/hwæt has singular morphology only. The masculine/feminine series is shared: hwā, hwæs, hwǣm, hwone; neuter hwæt, hwæs, hwǣm, hwæt. Do not invent plural or separate feminine forms. Cook also prints hwām for the dative; it is a valid recognized alternative to selected hwǣm.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Eight productive NGDA cells. Distinct hwȳ/hwon instrumentals remain reference; lexical hwȳ why is separately productive.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Use the full strong NGDA endings with each listed lexical stem: masculine singular zero/-es/-um/-ne; neuter zero/-es/-um/zero; feminine selected zero or -u/-re/-re/-e; masculine plural -e/-ra/-um/-e; neuter selected zero or -u/-ra/-um/zero or -u; feminine plural -a/-ra/-um/-a. Feminine plural -e is a valid broader strong-adjective alternative, already established in the course; the selected matrices consistently use -a. Gender/number/case still agree with the modified noun or referent.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Complete24 logical cells per selected strong model; distinct masculine/neuter singular instrumental -e is reference, not general instrumental production.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Selected feminine nominative singular and neuter nominative/accusative plural are sumu, but hwilc, hūlic, gehwilc, swilc and self. The selected ǣnig model retains -u as ǣnigu; the analogical zero-ending ǣnig is a recognized alternative. These listed outcomes govern production; a learner must not infer the entire disyllabic pattern from modern-looking spelling or from one familiar adjective.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Short sum has -u; heavy/selected zero-ending models and the explicit ǣnig alternative remain distinct. Cook and Wright state variation and analogy, so no universal spelling-only rule is asserted.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Hwæðer selects hwæðr- before the ordinary vowel endings: hwæðres, hwæðrum, hwæðre, hwæðra. Retain e before consonantal endings: hwæðerne, hwæðerre, hwæðerra. Feminine nominative singular and neuter nominative/accusative plural are hwæðer, not forms copied from prior ōðru. The earlier ōðer/ōðru paradigm retains its exact existing forms. Attested hwæðeres and simplified feminine hwæðere are valid variants; they do not replace the selected matrix.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Full strong morphology, including plural alternatives between groups. No conjunction whether or indefinite either syntax is inferred from interrogative morphology. Complete cells are model derivations, not claims of individual textual attestation.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: The selected transparent ǣnig model retains i throughout: ǣniges, ǣnigum, ǣnigne, ǣnigre, ǣnige, ǣnigra, ǣniga, and the listed ǣnigu cells. Disyllabic syncope is variable, with analogical restorations; do not mechanically contract every -ig adjective as hālig. Optional additional syncopated lexical spellings are not independently assigned here.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Full selected NGDA production. Extra dictionary text was a finding aid but its images were not obtained, so it is unused as evidence. No unsupported extra variant milestone.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Select Cook hwilc, hwæðer and hūlic. Hwelc/hwylc and expanded hwilcere/hwilcera are recorded variants. BT marks hūlīc; this is a separate source-edition spelling and does not silently change Cook's ū-only notation. Do not infer or add unprinted vowel length.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Selected-spelling recall versus acceptance of documented valid variants remains explicit.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Ilca is weak only. Its stem ilc- takes masculine nominative singular -a; feminine/neuter nominative singular and neuter accusative singular -e; other singular NGDA cells -an; plural nominative/accusative -an, genitive -ra, dative -um. Apply the same endings to self- for the weak self model; retain the separate strong self matrix.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Two complete24-cell weak systems. Weak-only ilca must not acquire an invented strong ilc paradigm. Weak instrumental is syncretic with dative and gains no general syntax here.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: Ðe is invariant. The inflected relative se/sēo/ðæt reuses every prior NGDA form, alone or followed by ðe. In the selected ordinary construction, its case follows its internal role while gender/number track the antecedent; the antecedent's external case can differ. In a possessive relative, genitive marks possession within the relative clause (English whose/of whom/of which); its gender and number still refer back to the antecedent, not to the possessed noun. This uses the already productive demonstrative genitives and does not promote earlier first/second-person personal genitives or general instrumentals. Case attraction is an attested recognition exception, not assigned production.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Ordinary subject, possessive, direct-object and governed/recipient functions; relative verb person/number follows the antecedent where relevant. ðe+personal pronoun is a bounded recognition strategy.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: The recognition ge-compound uses the interrogative-type singular pattern: gehwā/gehwæt, gehwæs, gehwǣm, gehwone/gehwæt. No plural is invented.
audited_inflection_rules.scope: Eight NGDA recognition cells; ordinary/partitive/distributive independent production remains Unit15. Other indefinite families have explicit dispositions.

audited_inflection_rules.rule: WeakII ætēowian keeps the lexical ætēow- stem. Present indicative ætēowie, ætēowast, ætēowað, plural ætēowiað; preterite ætēowode, ætēowodest, ætēowode, plural ætēowodon. Present subjunctive singular ætēowie/plural ætēowien; preterite singular ætēowode/plural ætēowoden. Every plural/subject-person cell is explicitly recorded. Cook allows -i-/ig(e)/g variants; exact p124 uses ætēowie without g.
